summary: Recorded the tick-period sweep and the condition it measured. CheckRun 10db1b327b784fb48711dec936afc73d (exit 0, three cases) evaluated all three comparisons and they separate cleanly: at 100 ms and 250 ms the obligation holds (the fresh call returned index 2, exactly where entry 33 sits, and that index held the caller's entry), while at 500 ms it is violated with a complete witness (returned index 4 while entry 33 sits at index 2 and index 4 holds entry 35). Together with the two 1000 ms runs the retained band is now 100/250 ms holding and 500/1000 ms violating, so the condition no longer rests on one point plus construction feedback, and I updated the knowledge entry's statement, conditions and executions accordingly. The sweep also exposed something I recorded rather than smoothed over: every shifting run reports the origin's decided index as 0 at the re-synchronisation sample and the new leader's own call unresolved, while every holding run reports decided index 1 and that call resolved — so the tick period is confounded with whether the re-election outran the re-synchronisation, and the account must not attribute the shift to the tick period alone. That confounding is now the discriminator's next step (a run that completes the re-synchronisation at a large tick, or one that holds the re-synchronisation until after the re-election); the boundary between 250 and 500 ms remains unlocated. No execution was requested this turn (validation reports execution_requested false).
